docs.text:
Cursor、Codex IDE 或独立 MCP 接入需要本地 Python 环境。克隆仓库后，推荐用 uv 创建带 pip 的 Python 3.12 环境： git clone https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC.git && printf '
%s
%s
' \ '如果 TOMC 对你有帮助，欢迎 Star 支持（自愿）：' 'https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC' cd TOMC uv venv --python 3.12 --seed .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e '.[mcp]' 上面的 Bash / Git Bash 命令会在克隆成功后显示一次自愿 Star 邀请。直接使用普通 git clone 不会显示；克隆完成不代表已经安装。 UV 首次使用可能需要联网下载 Python 和依赖。Codex 原生插件 ZIP 的用户直接运行下文的 install.py ，无需另建这份手动环境。Windows PowerShell 步骤继续见 接入指南 。 如果使用系统 Python，可将创建命令换成 python3 -m venv .venv 。Ubuntu/Debian 的系统 Python 需要匹配的 venv/ensurepip 组件；默认 Python 可先用 sudo apt install python3-venv 安装。本轮 Ubuntu 的系统 Python 缺少 ensurepip ，若先前因此只生成了部分环境，可运行： uv venv --python 3.12 --allow-existing --seed .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install -e '.[mcp]' 要同时使用本地 Demo，可改装 python -m pip install -e '.[demo,mcp]' ，再运行 python -m demo.app ，打开 http://127.0.0.1:7860 。本轮 Demo 验证环境为 Ubuntu 24.04.5、Python 3.12.13、Gradio 5.49.1 ；macOS 安装未在这轮重测。 Linux 验证与安装反馈 。
docs.title: Linux/macOS 的手动 MCP 环境

docs.text: 0.2.1 下载包由本仓库源码构建为 outputs/plugins/tomc-memory-0.2.1.mcpb 。它带有 TOMC 源码，采用官方 MCPB UV runtime，由支持该运行方式的客户端管理 Python 和依赖，创建独立环境。首次安装需要联网下载，并非离线安装包；用户不必先手动安装 Python。 官方 UV 安装包示例 维护者可以在仓库中构建和检查： python scripts/build_plugin.py python scripts/plugin_smoke.py outputs/plugins/tomc-memory-0.2.1.mcpb 第二条命令需要 uv 和 MCP 测试客户端（ .[mcp] ）。它在仓库外解压安装包并启动锁定的运行环境，不会安装到助手中，也不会更改助手配置。分享时提供 .mcpb 文件及其 .sha256 校验文件；不要把自己电脑生成的 Cursor 路径链接当成可移植安装包。 更新 Claude Desktop，取得 .mcpb 文件。 进入 Settings → Extensions → Advanced settings → Install Extension… 。 选择文件，查看说明并按提示确认安装。 开启对话，检查 TOMC 工具是否可用；0.2.1 共十个，包括四个新的只读上下文与状态工具。 这是 官方支持的自定义安装路径 。完成打包和 MCP 协议检查，并不等于已通过所有桌面环境验收；macOS、Windows 上的实际 Claude Desktop 安装仍需验证。
docs.title: Claude Desktop

docs.text: 安装 UV ，确保 uv 在 PATH 中。然后在 Claude Code 中运行： /plugin marketplace add ZipengWu365/TOMC /plugin install tomc-memory@tomc 新开会话或重新加载 VS Code 窗口，运行 /mcp ，服务显示为 plugin:tomc-memory:tomc 。插件目录是 plugins/claude-code ；首次启动会按需下载 Python 和锁定的 mcp 依赖。更新时先运行 claude plugin marketplace update tomc ，再运行 claude plugin update tomc-memory@tomc ；卸载用 claude plugin uninstall tomc-memory@tomc 。如果以前手动注册过 TOMC，请用 claude mcp remove tomc-memory --scope user 删除旧条目，避免出现两套工具。
docs.title: 作为插件安装（推荐）

docs.text: Claude Code 不能直接安装 .mcpb 文件，但可以把包里同一套锁定环境作为本地 stdio MCP 服务启动。 下载 tomc-memory-0.2.1.mcpb ，核对 SHA-256，再解压（它是 ZIP 格式）到一个会长期保留的目录。 安装 UV ，确保 uv 在 PATH 中，再运行下文的命令。将示例路径替换为实际解压目录；路径包含空格时保留引号。 运行 uv sync --locked --directory "/absolute/path/to/extracted" ，安装锁定的依赖。 注册服务，在所有项目中可用： bash claude mcp add tomc-memory --scope user -- uv run --locked --directory "/absolute/path/to/extracted" src/server.py 如果想把笔记本放在单独的数据库里，在 -- 前加上 -e TOMC_MEMORY_PATH="/absolute/path/to/memory.sqlite3" 。 claude mcp get tomc-memory 应显示 Connected 。 5. 新开一个 Claude Code 会话，或重新加载 VS Code 窗口，再输入 /mcp 。每个工具第一次使用时，Claude Code 会请求权限。 用 claude mcp remove tomc-memory --scope user 可以删除。请保留解压目录；移动目录后需要重新注册。
docs.title: 手动注册 MCP 运行环境

docs.text: 以下内容适用于所有操作系统，只是文件路径不同。 VS Code 里的 Claude Code 面板和 claude 命令是同一个 Claude Code，用 --scope user 注册的服务在面板里同样可用。注册后重新加载 VS Code 窗口，或新开一个会话即可。 如果 claude 不在 PATH 中，扩展自带的 CLI 位于 ~/.vscode/extensions/anthropic.claude-code-<版本>-<平台>/resources/native-binary/ 。在 Windows 上是 %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\anthropic.claude-code-<版本>-win32-x64\resources\native-binary\claude.exe 。用完整路径调用即可。 虚拟环境里的可执行文件，在 Windows 上位于 .venv/Scripts/ ，在 macOS 和 Linux 上位于 .venv/bin/ 。 如果当前激活了 conda 或其他虚拟环境，uv 会提示 VIRTUAL_ENV ... will be ignored 。这不影响使用： --directory 会选用包自己的环境。 会话进行中新加的服务，要到下一个会话才能用。
docs.title: VS Code 扩展注意事项

docs.text: 请求里要点名工具。 如果历史已经在对话里，Claude 会直接回答：工具调用无法缩减宿主已经持有的上下文。可以明确写： "用 tomc-memory 的 prepare_context 处理这段历史，task 是……，budget 设为 200，然后根据返回的 memory 回答。" 适合跨会话使用，或在 API 调用前使用。 用 remember_memory 保存长历史，之后在新会话里用 recall_memory 加上任务和预算取回；也可以在下一次 API 请求中改发准备好的上下文，代替完整历史。 预算要小于历史长度。 本来就放得下的历史会原样返回（ raw ）。 结构化记录需要支持的行格式： key = value 、 B copies A 和 x -[rel]-> y 。普通叙述可以作为挑选的原文保留；具体路由和输入节省取决于任务与预算。 来源编号是 TOMC 自己从 0 开始的行编号。 u0 是第一行非空文本；如果你的历史本身已经用 u1 、 u2 ……标号，两者会差一位。可以换别的标号，或者不标。 按历史长度选预算；历史超过约 10,000 token 才明显省钱。 Claude Code 每次请求自带约 39,000 个 token 的指令和工具定义，调用工具还会多出几次请求。VS Code 扩展实测中（模型为 Claude Opus 5.5），预算 8,192 在各长度下 5 题全对；此时从笔记本取回，和直接贴入 10K token 的历史费用相同，对 20K 和 40K token 的历史分别便宜 38% 和 65%。在接近 API 调用的请求中，同样预算让输入减少 9%、53% 和 77%。预算 1,024 让输入减少 85–96%，但会漏掉部分最新值：叙述形式的更新只能作为原文保留，小预算装不下所有更新。 没有验证过更小的预算，就用默认值。 不传 budget 时保留历史的约 80%（至少 1,024 个估算 token）。在三种长度、每种 3 份历史上，保留 50–80% 都 45 题全对，输入分别约减少 49%（50%）到 20%（80%）；只保留 10–20% 会漏掉最新值。想用更小的预算，先拿自己的一部分任务和完整历史对比确认。 长历史在聊天之外导入。 用 remember_memory 保存，模型得把整段历史作为工具参数重新输出一遍。建议改用插件自带的运行环境直接导入； TOMC_MEMORY_PATH 要和注册服务时一致（没设置就用默认数据库）： bash uv run --locked --directory <extracted> python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'src'); from tomc.store import MemoryStore; print(MemoryStore().remember('project', open(r'<history.txt>', encoding='utf-8').read()))" 每条历史最多 200,000 个字符，大约相当于 40,000 token 的英文聊天。 - 把准备好的内容当作不可信的证据。 保留原始历史，以便查看 TOMC 省略的细节。
docs.title: 使用技巧

docs.text: 先按 接入指南 在 TOMC 环境中安装 .[mcp] ，再使用该环境中的 Python 执行： python -m tomc setup --client cursor --link 打开生成的链接，在 Cursor 中确认添加。它使用你当前安装环境中 Python 的绝对路径，因此需要保留该环境，移动后重新生成链接。命令本身只打印链接，不会改写客户端配置。 Cursor 官方支持安装链接，但这个链接只添加 MCP 配置，不负责安装 TOMC、Python 或依赖。一个人在自己电脑上生成的路径链接，不能当作所有人都能使用的安装包。 Cursor 官方安装链接说明
docs.title: Cursor

docs.text: 按 Cursor / TRAE 接入指南 ，在设置 → MCP → 添加 → 手动添加中注册锁定依赖的本地运行环境。最新源码也支持 python -m tomc setup --client trae 。这是手动 MCP 接入；Claude 插件 manifest 不是 TRAE 安装器。客户端工具发现和模型调用尚未验证。
docs.title: TRAE

docs.text: 按 WorkBuddy 接入指南 ，通过插件 → MCP 服务器 → 配置 MCP 注册锁定依赖的本地运行环境。最新源码也支持 python -m tomc setup --client workbuddy 。配置使用 .workbuddy/mcp.json 。客户端工具发现与模型调用尚未验证；目前是手动 MCP 接入，尚未上架腾讯市场。
docs.title: 腾讯 WorkBuddy

docs.text: 0.2.1 下载包构建为 outputs/plugins/tomc-memory-codex-0.2.1.zip 。它包含 .agents/plugins/marketplace.json 本地市场目录、 install.py 安装助手，以及 plugins/tomc-memory/ 插件：其中有官方支持的 .codex-plugin/plugin.json 兼容 manifest、与 Claude 包相同的锁定 TOMC 运行环境和记忆 skill。兼容 manifest 声明随包提供的工具和 skill，安装助手则为当前安装生成启动路径。可以私下分享原始 ZIP，这并不意味着 TOMC 已上线公开插件目录。 OpenAI 官方插件打包与本地市场说明 维护者可以在仓库中运行 python scripts/build_codex_plugin.py 构建候选包，再分享 ZIP 及其 .sha256 校验文件。 使用支持插件的新版本 Codex CLI，并按 官方说明安装 UV 。与 Claude Desktop 自动管理 UV 扩展不同，这个包需要已有的 UV 可执行文件。TOMC 需要 Python 3.10 或更新版本，macOS 的系统 Python 可能过旧。无需单独安装兼容 Python：下面的命令让 UV 提供 Python 3.12 和依赖，因此首次启动需要联网。 将 ZIP 解压到准备长期保留的目录。 在包含 install.py 的解压目录中打开终端，执行： uv run --no-project --python 3.12 install.py --check uv run --no-project --python 3.12 install.py 新开 Codex 会话，检查 TOMC 工具是否可用。 --check 检查包文件、可执行文件路径和 Codex 插件支持，不写入配置或注册插件。可执行文件不在 PATH 中时，把占位路径替换为这台电脑的实际路径： "/absolute/path/to/uv" run --no-project --python 3.12 install.py \ --uv "/absolute/path/to/uv" --codex "/absolute/path/to/codex" 安装助手会解析这台电脑上 UV 和运行环境的绝对路径，更新解压目录中的候选包启动配置，再调用官方 Codex 市场注册和插件安装命令。它不会整份覆盖已有的 Codex 配置。生成的路径属于当前安装，移动解压目录后需要重新运行助手。分享时请使用原始 ZIP，不要分享包含自己电脑路径的已配置副本。 需要独立记忆本时，在安装命令后加 --store /path/to/notebooks.sqlite3 ，为 Codex 的 MCP 进程显式设置数据库路径；默认仍为 ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 。
docs.title: Codex

docs.text: 在 PowerShell 中查看终端实际选择的程序： Get-Command codex | Select-Object Source codex --version Get-Command uv | Select-Object Source uv --version PATH 中的 CLI 可能与桌面应用内置引擎不同。安装助手默认选择 PATH 中的 CLI；需要指定其他程序时，用 --codex ，并将下面占位路径换成真实路径： uv run --no-project install.py --codex 'C:\path\to\codex.exe' 目标 host 应同时支持插件命令和你的模型账户。安装成功提示说明完成了注册，不代表模型请求一定成功。新开会话后，先检查 TOMC 工具（0.2.1 共十个），再运行 准备例子 。明确要求调用 prepare_context ，并查看实际工具结果。 Windows 反馈 分别记录安装、运行和真实模型试用。 若只希望生成本地启动配置、打印后续安装命令，而不注册市场或安装插件，可以执行： uv run --no-project --python 3.12 install.py --configure-only 市场注册后，也可以在支持的 Codex CLI 中输入 /plugins ，浏览该市场并安装 TOMC。 官方插件命令 、 插件浏览器 Codex IDE 扩展目前不支持原生插件。IDE 用户或没有插件命令的旧版 CLI 用户，可以按 接入指南 安装 .[mcp] ，再用该环境中的 Python 生成配置： python -m tomc setup --client codex 将打印出的条目加入 MCP 设置。也可以使用 CLI 直接注册已安装的 Python，将占位路径替换为实际路径： codex mcp add tomc -- /absolute/path/to/installed/python -m tomc mcp Codex CLI 和 IDE 均支持直接 MCP 接入。同一客户端中，原生插件与单独注册的 TOMC 服务二选一，避免工具重复。 官方 MCP 接入说明 2026-10-04，已发布 preview.4 ZIP 通过桌面内置 CLI 0.160.0，作为原生插件长期安装到这台 Windows 的 Codex 个人配置中。原有 gpt-6.1-sol 模型、OpenAI provider 和登录完成两次模型回合、四次 TOMC 调用：第一段聊天准备、保存并取回；独立新聊天只收到记忆本名称和任务，也取回成功。准备和取回都没有传入预算参数，使用新默认值；两段回答均给出正确的当前值 FastAPI 与复制快照 Flask。没有配置、feature、MCP server 或工具 namespace 覆盖设置，其他插件保持启用。安装目录长期保留在 ~/.codex/tomc/assistant-preview.4 ，UV 位于 ~/.codex/tomc/tools/Scripts/uv.exe 。 合成记忆本实际保存到默认 ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 ，完整 host 重启后仍可取回，随后被精确删除。保存前和删除后的 host 列表均为空，独立只读 SQLite 检查确认最终零条目。正常存取使数据库元数据发生变化；安装后的配置和认证元数据保持不变。桌面 GUI 安装按钮仍未逐步点击验收。具体条件及证据见 Windows 反馈 与 preview.4 验证记录 。移除插件不会删除已有记忆本。 历史 2026-10-02 的检查范围更窄：preview.2 和 preview.3 在 Windows CLI 0.146.0、0.159.2 的隔离配置中通过完整安装及实际 host 工具检查，没有模型调用；preview.1 的模型准备及新聊天取回使用临时 MCP 设置与直接开放工具。这些条件按原日期保留，不代表上文的 preview.4 安装。Claude Desktop 与 Cursor 仍只有运行检查。 本轮 Linux 使用 Codex CLI 0.159.0-alpha.12.1 对 preview.2 验证了原生插件安装及 MCP 工具，并检查 .mcpb 的后端运行。检查仅使用临时配置和记忆库，没有调用模型；Claude/Cursor GUI 安装、个人配置中的永久安装以及模型自动使用工具仍未验证。此前 Windows 的模型调用结果与本轮 Linux 协议检查分别报告，不互相替代。 Linux 验证记录 。 2026-10-02 下载的 preview.2 ZIP 在 macOS 26.3 arm64、Codex CLI 0.159.2 上作为原生插件安装并启用。模型实际调用其 prepare_context 工具，正确回答当前值 FastAPI 与此前复制的 Flask 快照。已安装的客户端提供全部五个工具；独立数据库上的中文笔记经进程重启仍可取回，也能删除。这台 Mac 原先没有 UV，系统 Python 为 3.9.6，因此需要先准备兼容运行环境。Codex、Claude Desktop、Cursor 的 GUI 安装仍未验收。 macOS 安装与使用技巧 · 验证记录 。 历史 Windows preview.1 排查中，npm Codex CLI 0.146.0 可以安装插件，但原默认模型请求返回 HTTP 400；桌面内置 CLI 0.159.2 则支持相同模型和登录。应指定预期可执行文件，不要假设 PATH 中的 CLI 就是桌面引擎。
docs.title: Windows：先检查目标 Codex

docs.text: 使用安装时同一个 Codex 可执行文件： codex plugin remove tomc-memory@tomc-local codex plugin marketplace remove tomc-local 停止 TOMC 会话后可删除试用解压目录。若使用 --store ，确认笔记不再需要后，可选择删除该独立测试数据库。卸载保留默认 ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 ；不要仅为卸载插件而删除已有记忆本。如需删除某个记忆本，可先调用 forget_memory 再卸载。
docs.title: 试用后移除原生插件

docs.text: 日常使用可以参考 使用技巧 ：具体任务、更新顺序、原文核对和 notebook 提示词。 安装后，让助手调用 TOMC 的 prepare_context 工具：把下面的文本传给 history ，将 task 设为 "当前 framework 和 backup_framework 的值是什么？" ， budget 设为 64 ，再让助手根据返回的记忆回答。 framework = Flask backup_framework copies framework framework = FastAPI Monday notes: the team reviewed the project backlog, discussed deployment windows and agreed to keep the public API routes and response fields unchanged during the refactor. Tuesday notes: the migration plan still needs a review from the database owner, and the pagination tests have not yet been written or run. Wednesday notes: the team checked the release checklist, added a rollback task, and postponed the documentation update until after the test results are available. 这个例子使用显式赋值和复制。TOMC 准备 framework = FastAPI 、 backup_framework = Flask 两条记录，并保留来源链接。是否调用工具由客户端控制，回答由原来的模型生成。 MCP 的 prepare_context 默认保存成功准备的结果和任务，可关闭上下文记录。它不另外复制全部原始历史，但已能放进预算的历史可能完整保留在快照中；较长的普通文本可以使用检索，不一定产生结构化记录。 budget 按词法计数器限制记忆文本，任务和工具消息框架还会增加输入。 上面的 64-token 预算是明确指定的小例子。使用当前默认值时，省略 budget ：TOMC 按历史 lexical 估算长度的约 80% 选择预算，最低为 1,024；本来就放得下的历史原样保留。这不是固定节省比例。 每次 MCP 结果都能放进一次工具输出。客户端会截断过长的工具结果，所以 TOMC 自己在约 20,000 字符内保留最相关的内容（Claude Code 通过 hook 标明身份时为 50,000），可用 TOMC_MCP_MAX_CHARS 调整。对笔记和文档，如果问题的证据很明确，结果还可能小于预算。同一聊天里再次处理同一份来源时，助手可以把上次的 delivery.id 作为 since_delivery_id 传入：TOMC 只返回改动、删除或新相关的行，没有变化时只返回一句说明。新聊天、重启后的服务或过期的 ID 会拿到完整上下文。
docs.title: 准备上下文

docs.text: 应用请求使用 prepared.messages 替换原历史；助手中可以把准备后的文本交给新聊天。在已有长聊天里调用 TOMC，不会清除客户端保存的原消息，因此一次工具调用本身并不代表节省了 token。插件不会全局拦截 API 请求。衡量节省量时，用模型的 tokenizer 检查完整输入；保留原历史，以便查看结果未包含的细节。 先核对选中的原文、来源链接和计算出的状态，再交给模型。Demo 的 Small request 面向短记录示例；普通段落可在 Memory size 中选择 Balanced 或 More detail ，并展开 How this context was prepared 查看结果。预算太小可能放不下完整原文行，不能把空上下文当作成功压缩。
docs.title: 在下一次调用中使用更少的上下文

docs.text: 工具 用途 prepare_context 按任务处理历史；开启上下文记录时保存结果和任务 remember_memory 将传入的笔记追加到指定记忆本 recall_memory 为当前任务取回指定记忆本 list_memories 查看记忆本名称，不返回内容 forget_memory 按要求删除指定记忆本 get_usage_stats 查看累计、今日或最近七天（UTC）的本地上下文估算减少量 get_status 只读查看设置、配置证据和最近准备状态 list_contexts 列出已保存的上下文快照，不返回正文 get_context 读取选定快照，作为可能不完整的历史证据 make_handoff 返回自包含接续提示词，不发送消息 可选：跨聊天保存与取回历史 记忆本保存传入的原始文本； recall_memory 在取回时按任务准备上下文。 prepare_context 不需要记忆本。自 0.2.0 起，在开启上下文记录时，会将这两条准备路径的成功结果和任务保存为独立快照。
docs.title: 工具

docs.text: 第一段对话： 请用 TOMC 把这些笔记保存到 workshop：研讨会人数现为 28 人，B 会议室有空但尚未预订，还需确认无障碍设施。 新开一段对话： 从 TOMC 取回 workshop，告诉我接下来需要确认什么。 助手决定是否调用工具，并遵循客户端的权限设置；保存笔记不会替你预订会议室，也不会把待确认事项变成已完成。
docs.title: 用两次对话试一下

docs.text: 要从 Codex 切到 Claude Code 继续，或反过来，让两边的 TOMC 服务使用同一数据库，并传入同一记忆本名称。 共享路径设置与两段接续提示词 。 默认记忆存放在用户目录的 ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 ，不放在安装包中。同一台电脑上使用同一数据库的客户端可以共享记忆；不同路径则相互独立。笔记以本地明文存储，取回后进入助手上下文，遵循助手平台的数据政策；卸载插件不会自动删除数据库。 插件只看到传给工具的内容，不会自动读取全部聊天、拦截 API 请求或替换客户端的上下文窗口。这个日常使用接口采用 Demo 的任务路由和本地记忆本，并非论文 BEAM 实验的精确配置；论文分数不能直接当作此插件流程的效果保证。
docs.title: 存储与能力范围

docs.text: 准备和召回会返回本次上下文估算减少量，供助手显示。 get_usage_stats 可查询累计、今天和最近七天（UTC）。数字统计本身不含原文或任务；自 0.2.0 起默认另外保存准备结果正文与任务，可关闭上下文记录。不上传遥测，这些数字也不是实际 API 或账单节省；旧的纯数字历史无法还原正文。已有安装需更新运行时并开启新会话或按宿主支持方式重载。 统计口径与使用方法 。
docs.title: 上下文减少统计（0.1.2）

docs.text:
Use TOMC with your assistant The MCP server lets an assistant prepare supplied history for its next task. Your existing assistant writes the answer. Named notebooks optionally keep notes across chats. This integration uses the official Python MCP SDK and clients that launch local stdio servers. It provides explicit local persistence alongside the stateless compiler. It does not automatically capture your chats. Claude Desktop and Codex CLI have installation candidates that include a locked local runtime. Cursor users can generate an install link after installing the environment. See Install TOMC in your assistant ; desktop GUI acceptance is still pending. The manual setup below also supports the Codex IDE extension. Install The repository is public. There is no published PyPI package or official public marketplace listing. git clone https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC.git && printf '
%s
%s
' \ 'If TOMC helps with your work, consider a Star on GitHub (optional):' 'https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC' cd TOMC The Bash / Git Bash command above prints an optional Star invitation after a successful clone. Plain git clone does not show it; cloning alone does not install TOMC. On Linux/macOS, use UV to install Python and seed pip. This path passed the Linux check: uv venv --python 3.12 --seed .venv source .venv/bin/activate Alternatively, create the environment with python3 -m venv .venv and activate it as above. Debian/Ubuntu need the matching python3-venv package; a system without it can report that ensurepip is unavailable. For a partially created environment, use uv venv --python 3.12 --allow-existing --seed .venv . In Windows PowerShell with Python 3.12 installed: py -3.12 -m venv .venv On Linux/macOS, install with the activated environment's interpreter: python -m pip install -e '.[mcp]' On Windows PowerShell, use the environment's Python directly. Activation is unnecessary: .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e '.[mcp]' .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m tomc setup --client cursor --link Change cursor --link to codex , claude , trae or workbuddy to print that client's configuration. A Cursor link registers the environment you just installed; it does not install dependencies on another computer. You can also install with uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e '.[mcp]' . On Windows, use .venv\Scripts\python.exe . The Linux verification report records fresh installation, actual Codex tool discovery and packaged MCP runtime checks. Core and MCP require Python 3.10+. The integration pins the SDK's v1.30 maintenance line , which also works with the current Gradio demo on Python 3.10–3.13. SDK 2.x requires a Pydantic version that conflicts with this demo version. CI checks combined installations on Python 3.10 and 3.12; requirements-mcp.lock records the standalone MCP dependencies. Connect your client Run these commands using the installed environment's python . They print configuration containing the absolute interpreter path. Merge the TOMC entry into your existing settings. Client Generate configuration Destination Codex python -m tomc setup --client codex ~/.codex/config.toml or MCP settings Claude Desktop python -m tomc setup --client claude Settings → Developer → Edit Config; add mcpServers.tomc Cursor python -m tomc setup --client cursor Project .cursor/mcp.json or user ~/.cursor/mcp.json ; add mcpServers.tomc TRAE (International / CN) python -m tomc setup --client trae Settings → MCP → Add → Create Manually, local environment; or enable project MCP and use .trae/mcp.json Tencent WorkBuddy python -m tomc setup --client workbuddy User ~/.workbuddy/mcp.json or project .workbuddy/mcp.json ; Plugins → MCP Servers → Configure MCP For manually entered Cursor STDIO configuration, add "type": "stdio" alongside command and args , or use the client-specific template linked below. The TRAE option is available in the current source checkout; older packaged runtimes do not include this setup alias. TRAE requires an executable command path without spaces. For the locked UV runtime, copyable JSON and client-specific steps, see Cursor / TRAE setup . Cursor and TRAE client tool calls remain unverified. The WorkBuddy option is available in the current source checkout. It declares local stdio and keeps the selected store path in the launch arguments. See WorkBuddy setup for the locked UV template. WorkBuddy client tool calls remain unverified. Codex CLI users on macOS/Linux can also register the server directly: codex mcp add tomc -- "$PWD/.venv/bin/python" -m tomc mcp For the same direct MCP registration from the repository directory in Windows PowerShell: $tomcPython = (Resolve-Path .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe).Path codex mcp add tomc -- $tomcPython -m tomc mcp These commands register the server in Codex. Use this path or the native plugin in the same client, to avoid duplicate tools. The command syntax follows the official Codex MCP guide , checked on 2026-10-02. Reconnect the client, open a new chat and check that five TOMC tools appear. The client launches the server. A separate tomc mcp terminal is unnecessary; a stdio server waiting silently in a terminal is normal. The configuration examples follow the Codex , Claude Desktop and Cursor guides reviewed on 2026-09-09. Subprocess tests cover tool discovery, calls and legacy initialization. Individual product GUIs were not tested end to end. Try two chats Start with usage tips for task-specific preparation and checking the returned sources. The Windows installation feedback separates installation, runtime and model checks. In the first chat: Use TOMC to remember this as workshop : the workshop now has 28 attendees. Room B is available but not booked. We still need to confirm accessibility. In a new chat: Recall workshop from TOMC and help me continue. The assistant uses remember_memory and recall_memory , subject to its tool-permission settings. The notebook stores the supplied notes. TOMC does not book Room B or mark accessibility as confirmed. To find a notebook, ask “List my TOMC notebooks.” To delete one, ask “Forget the TOMC notebook workshop.” The delete tool removes only that exact name and is marked destructive. Storage and privacy Each save appends the supplied text; an immediate identical retry is deduplicated. Notebook names stay separate. Recall keeps short histories intact and routes longer histories for the current task. The default database is ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 . Set TOMC_MEMORY_PATH to change it, or generate configuration with a custom path: python -m tomc setup --client cursor --store /absolute/path/memory.sqlite3 Clients using the same database share notebooks. Separate database paths keep environments separate. Each notebook accepts up to 200,000 characters; an append that exceeds the limit fails without removing existing entries. Submitted text is stored as local plaintext. Recalled context is sent back to the assistant and follows that host's data policy. Deleting a notebook does not erase an assistant's chat or guarantee forensic erasure. The server reads only text passed to its tools. It does not read other chats, browse files, run stored commands or call a model. It exposes no HTTP endpoint. The hosted demo has no shared notebook service, and this configuration does not connect remote-only clients such as ChatGPT web. Copy and paste instead Use Use now , or prepare a prompt from the command line: python -m tomc prepare demo/examples/preferences.json --task "What are the current preferences?" Add --messages for provider-neutral message JSON, --output outputs/context.txt to save the prompt, or use - as the filename to read stdin. This path creates no notebook and calls no model. If the client cannot find the executable, regenerate its entry from the installed environment. For an import error, install .[mcp] there. Regenerate configuration after moving or deleting the virtual environment.

On Windows, use .venv\Scripts\python.exe . The Linux verification report records fresh installation, actual Codex tool discovery and packaged MCP runtime checks. Core and MCP require Python 3.10+. The integration pins the SDK's v1.30 maintenance line , which also works with the current Gradio demo on Python 3.10–3.13. SDK 2.x requires a Pydantic version that conflicts with this demo version. CI checks combined installations on Python 3.10 and 3.12; requirements-mcp.lock records the standalone MCP dependencies.

docs.text: Run these commands using the installed environment's python . They print configuration containing the absolute interpreter path. Merge the TOMC entry into your existing settings. Client Generate configuration Destination Codex python -m tomc setup --client codex ~/.codex/config.toml or MCP settings Claude Desktop python -m tomc setup --client claude Settings → Developer → Edit Config; add mcpServers.tomc Cursor python -m tomc setup --client cursor Project .cursor/mcp.json or user ~/.cursor/mcp.json ; add mcpServers.tomc TRAE (International / CN) python -m tomc setup --client trae Settings → MCP → Add → Create Manually, local environment; or enable project MCP and use .trae/mcp.json Tencent WorkBuddy python -m tomc setup --client workbuddy User ~/.workbuddy/mcp.json or project .workbuddy/mcp.json ; Plugins → MCP Servers → Configure MCP For manually entered Cursor STDIO configuration, add "type": "stdio" alongside command and args , or use the client-specific template linked below. The TRAE option is available in the current source checkout; older packaged runtimes do not include this setup alias. TRAE requires an executable command path without spaces. For the locked UV runtime, copyable JSON and client-specific steps, see Cursor / TRAE setup . Cursor and TRAE client tool calls remain unverified. The WorkBuddy option is available in the current source checkout. It declares local stdio and keeps the selected store path in the launch arguments. See WorkBuddy setup for the locked UV template. WorkBuddy client tool calls remain unverified. Codex CLI users on macOS/Linux can also register the server directly: codex mcp add tomc -- "$PWD/.venv/bin/python" -m tomc mcp For the same direct MCP registration from the repository directory in Windows PowerShell: $tomcPython = (Resolve-Path .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe).Path codex mcp add tomc -- $tomcPython -m tomc mcp These commands register the server in Codex. Use this path or the native plugin in the same client, to avoid duplicate tools. The command syntax follows the official Codex MCP guide , checked on 2026-10-02. Reconnect the client, open a new chat and check that five TOMC tools appear. The client launches the server. A separate tomc mcp terminal is unnecessary; a stdio server waiting silently in a terminal is normal. The configuration examples follow the Codex , Claude Desktop and Cursor guides reviewed on 2026-09-09. Subprocess tests cover tool discovery, calls and legacy initialization. Individual product GUIs were not tested end to end.
docs.title: Connect your client

docs.text: Start with usage tips for task-specific preparation and checking the returned sources. The Windows installation feedback separates installation, runtime and model checks. In the first chat: Use TOMC to remember this as workshop : the workshop now has 28 attendees. Room B is available but not booked. We still need to confirm accessibility. In a new chat: Recall workshop from TOMC and help me continue. The assistant uses remember_memory and recall_memory , subject to its tool-permission settings. The notebook stores the supplied notes. TOMC does not book Room B or mark accessibility as confirmed. To find a notebook, ask “List my TOMC notebooks.” To delete one, ask “Forget the TOMC notebook workshop.” The delete tool removes only that exact name and is marked destructive.
docs.title: Try two chats

docs.text: Each save appends the supplied text; an immediate identical retry is deduplicated. Notebook names stay separate. Recall keeps short histories intact and routes longer histories for the current task. The default database is ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 . Set TOMC_MEMORY_PATH to change it, or generate configuration with a custom path: python -m tomc setup --client cursor --store /absolute/path/memory.sqlite3 Clients using the same database share notebooks. Separate database paths keep environments separate. Each notebook accepts up to 200,000 characters; an append that exceeds the limit fails without removing existing entries. Submitted text is stored as local plaintext. Recalled context is sent back to the assistant and follows that host's data policy. Deleting a notebook does not erase an assistant's chat or guarantee forensic erasure. The server reads only text passed to its tools. It does not read other chats, browse files, run stored commands or call a model. It exposes no HTTP endpoint. The hosted demo has no shared notebook service, and this configuration does not connect remote-only clients such as ChatGPT web.
docs.title: Storage and privacy

docs.text: Use Use now , or prepare a prompt from the command line: python -m tomc prepare demo/examples/preferences.json --task "What are the current preferences?" Add --messages for provider-neutral message JSON, --output outputs/context.txt to save the prompt, or use - as the filename to read stdin. This path creates no notebook and calls no model. If the client cannot find the executable, regenerate its entry from the installed environment. For an import error, install .[mcp] there. Regenerate configuration after moving or deleting the virtual environment.

docs.text: Results and limitations The current snapshot was exported on 2026-09-28 from manuscript commit 7399657 . Paper results contains the complete tables and source references. What the experiments show Evidence Finding Conditions BEAM answer quality Higher TOMC means in all 18 overall and all 36 long-history comparisons at 500K/1M Three readers, six evaluated baseline configurations; these are mean comparisons BEAM reader input Overall savings of 34.77% vs LIGHT and 34.35% vs LLMLingua-2-H Equal mean of reader-wise ratios on matched valid questions Ten BEAM abilities Higher TOMC means than BEAM-RAG and LIGHT for temporal reasoning, extraction, contradiction resolution, multi-session reasoning and event ordering Three-way common valid set; equal mean of 500K/1M ability scores Construction 4.21 s/call on CPU, no auxiliary neural inference; 3.75 GiB peak process RSS Six replays; imports, input loading and tokenizer warm-up excluded Repaired NIAH pair Mean F1 of 87.28 with extra source and 82.26 without it; removal saves about 43%–44% input Separate batch with byte-identical compiled records VT state diagnostic 100% item recall for all three readers Full-history state replay, including after candidate removal Construction does not require changing or retraining the reader. Answer quality and input length depend on the task, selected evidence and reader. Baseline memory and TOMC memory The main BEAM comparisons use the same reader model on both sides. Each score pair is Baseline / TOMC : the named baseline's memory and TOMC's memory, evaluated on matched questions with matched scoring. TOMC's API integration lets an existing model read the prepared context. It is separate from combining TOMC with another memory method, which these comparisons do not evaluate. The compilation ablation asks a different question. It compares Full TOMC / TOMC w/o compilation , removing reader-visible records and their instructions while keeping source text and upstream routing fixed, without refilling the budget. The RULER component tests are also separate. They remove extra source on NIAH/QA2 or candidate rows on VT. VT remains a state-route diagnostic. Compare paired cells BEAM plans 600 questions per method and reader: 60 conversations, three history lengths and ten abilities. Each baseline comparison has its own valid paired set and scoring protocol. Compare within a score pair; TOMC's absolute numbers across protocol rows are not one shared scoring scale. The memory cap is 8,192 cl100k_base tokens. API reader input also includes the question and prompt overhead. “1M history” describes the original history, not a million-token reader request. Input changes average reader-wise ratios equally. The long-history summary pools valid questions within each reader before averaging relative changes. Ability plots instead average the 500K and 1M ability means equally. BEAM-RAG is the evaluated BGE single-route dense-retrieval configuration with pair chunks, top-five retrieval and budget packing. It differs from the demo's line-level BM25 rag and the historical Hybrid-RAG control. BRIEF-Pro uses archived hybrid-retrieval candidates. LIGHT uses writer/filter, remote summarization and budget packing. Results that limit the interpretation At 100K, Flash's mean scores are 61.01 for LIGHT and 58.21 for TOMC. On the common long-history ability set, TOMC trails both controls on instruction following, BEAM-RAG on abstention and LIGHT on summarization. Direct LLMLingua-2 has 200 empty memories at 1M, already empty before its guard. Their scores remain included. The low input reflects this unresolved failure, rather than effective compression. The BEAM compilation ablation changes mean quality by +1.20 points for GPT-5.1, −0.91 for Rednote and +3.01 for Flash. These protocol-matched results use separate dated batches. Temporal reasoning improves for all three, while event ordering declines for all three. Archived NIAH packing removed compiled blocks from the full condition as well as the source-removal condition. The full condition's 88.30 mean F1 therefore reflects retained source text; the removal's zero is a packing failure. The repaired pair is a separate batch. Flash's 100→99 repaired gap comes from one prespecified non-needle sample; both conditions score 100 on the other 99. Full-history VT replay reaches 100% recall with or without candidate rows. Compilation from selected evidence alone reaches about 20.4–20.6%, exposing missing dependencies. On QA2, raw text from the same selected evidence outperforms records alone and records plus raw for all three readers. Full TOMC scores 40.85 versus Query's 47.49; removing extra source lowers mean F1 to 8.44. Higher means do not establish significance in every comparison. TOMC also uses more input than several baselines. Quality and input are separate measurements. Construction measurements The table records per-call, per-conversation and batch construction stages. Ratios describe those stages; they are not matched end-to-end speedups. GPU allocation and process RSS are separate observed maxima. LIGHT's worker measurement includes its KV pool and excludes BGE and remote summarization. It is not a minimum GPU requirement. LLMLingua-2 was measured on CUDA but can be configured differently. TOMC does not have the lowest host RAM measurement. Reader inference and judging are outside the construction measurements. Demo limitations The normalized parser supports defined operations rather than arbitrary natural-language state extraction. The router uses keyword rules; BM25 uses lexical overlap. Negation, paraphrases and ambiguous references can lead to missed evidence or an unsuitable route. Source references make a retained record inspectable, but do not establish that its interpretation is correct. Row caps and budget packing can omit information. Check sources for important updates and retain raw text when wording matters. Demo token counts and caller-supplied prices estimate memory size and cost. They do not measure reader accuracy or actual billing. The audit ledger is outside the reader request. Model aliases can change, so a new API run may use a different model snapshot. Historical results The September 4 four-reader Hybrid-RAG batch remains in benchmarks/HISTORICAL_BEAM.md , with its original scores, intervals and missingness analysis. It is separate from the current main comparisons. Older boundary summaries remain in benchmarks/aggregate_results/boundaries.csv : IterCOMP multihop favors the control; LongMemEval-V2 ties BGE hybrid at 0.1074; LongBench-v2 full 503 scores 33.0%; UltraLongMix differences are nonsignificant. These are archived summaries, not newly recomputed current-paper results.

docs.text: Windows Codex: context budgets and actual input — 2026-10-05 中文报告 · Recorded data · Budget tips All four conditions answered 45/45 latest-project-state questions correctly. Compared with full history, 40%, 60% and default 80% history budgets reduced reported request input by a mean paired 29.7%, 19.5% and 9.2%. Preparation used the installed TOMC MCP tool on CPU, followed by one answering turn in a new Codex chat. Overall results Each condition has nine answering turns and 45 checked values. Input means are rounded to the nearest token; the JSON preserves unrounded means, each answer and its usage receipt. Context sent Mean provider input tokens Mean paired input reduction Checked values Full history 42,191 Reference 45/45 TOMC · 40% history budget 28,713 29.7% 45/45 TOMC · 60% history budget 33,344 19.5% 45/45 TOMC · default 80% history budget 38,035 9.2% 45/45 For each history, reduction is 100 × (1 − prepared_input / full_input) . The reported percentage averages those nine ratios equally. It is not the percentage change calculated from the two condition means; that would give longer histories more weight. Results by history length Each length has three histories and 15 checked values per condition. The labels describe approximate history lengths under cl100k_base , not complete request input or TOMC's lexical budget count. History length Context sent Mean provider input tokens Mean paired input reduction Checked values ~10K Full history 29,023 Reference 15/15 ~10K TOMC · 40% budget 23,195 20.1% 15/15 ~10K TOMC · 60% budget 25,160 13.3% 15/15 ~10K TOMC · default 80% 27,134 6.5% 15/15 ~20K Full history 38,846 Reference 15/15 ~20K TOMC · 40% budget 27,258 29.8% 15/15 ~20K TOMC · 60% budget 31,220 19.6% 15/15 ~20K TOMC · default 80% 35,173 9.5% 15/15 ~40K Full history 58,705 Reference 15/15 ~40K TOMC · 40% budget 35,687 39.2% 15/15 ~40K TOMC · 60% budget 43,651 25.6% 15/15 ~40K TOMC · default 80% 51,797 11.8% 15/15 What was tested The answering reader was gpt-6.1-sol ; Codex supplied the surrounding instructions, tools and session handling. The full-history control also kept TOMC and the other plugins installed. This is an evidence comparison within the same host, not a plugin-installed versus plugin-uninstalled comparison. Paper readers and coding-agent hosts . The Windows desktop-bundled Codex CLI was 0.160.0, using the existing gpt-6.1-sol model, OpenAI provider and ultra effort. Preview.4 was already installed in the actual personal profile. The three checked preparation sources ( easy.py , mcp_server.py , compiler.py ) matched repository commit ad89208 . Personal configuration stayed unchanged; no feature, MCP or tool-namespace override was used. The harness gave every condition the same developer instruction to answer from supplied evidence without tools. The corpus uses seeds 11, 23 and 37, each at 670, 1,340 and 2,700 chat turns. Histories contain ordinary prose updates and distractors. Five questions ask for the current deadline, page limit, evaluation owner, weekly meeting time and presentation venue. Lengths within a seed are nested. The 45 values therefore come from nine related histories and three seeds, rather than 45 independent projects. For each history, the harness called the native MCP prepare_context tool outside the answering model. The 40% and 60% budgets were the history's lexical estimate multiplied by 0.40 or 0.60 and rounded down. The 80% condition omitted budget , exercising the unchanged max(1024, ceil(history_estimate × 0.8)) default. Actual mean lexical evidence retention was 39.98%, 59.96% and 79.97%. All 27 prepared contexts selected tomc_raw and contained source blocks, with no STATE , REL or COUNT records. The ordinary-prose histories exercised source-selection fallback; this test does not independently validate operation compilation. Each full or prepared evidence packet then went into its own fresh ephemeral answering thread. All 36 answering turns completed, with no observed tool calls or model reroutes. Notebook saving and recall were not used. Asking an assistant to prepare or recall inside a chat adds model turns, which these single-answer figures do not include. Telemetry does not rule out hidden transport retries. How tokens and answers were checked Input is the final Codex inputTokens count, including cached input, host instructions and available tool definitions. Cached input is a subset of this total and is not subtracted. No estimated host overhead is removed. cl100k_base counts in the JSON describe supplied text; they are not asserted to be the provider's tokenizer. outputTokens includes reasoningOutputTokens ; both fields are recorded, and they must not be added together. This report makes no currency-cost or speedup claim. Answers were checked against the generator's current values, with normalized strings and recognized page-cap paraphrases. The page-limit check tests the stated numerical value; it does not distinguish inclusive from exclusive limits. The JSON retains original grading alongside the checked values. These descriptive results cover synthetic latest-state questions with one model, not general coding ability or a guarantee that a smaller budget preserves every fact. Choose a budget 40% produced the smallest tested requests; 60% leaves more room for evidence. Both are options to compare with full history on your own tasks. The default remains 80%. Use the Python example and MCP instructions to set an absolute budget, then inspect retained evidence and check the answer. The Claude Code results used Claude Opus 5.5 and a separate request workflow. Its approximately 20% default-input reduction should not be substituted for the Codex result. Reproduce the comparison Check the published record offline first. This needs Python 3.11 or later, with no account, installed plugin, MCP host or model request: python scripts/benchmarks/codex_retention_report.py --verify-published docs/validation_data/windows_codex_retention_20261005.json It regenerates the synthetic corpus and checks history hashes, expected values, saved answers, usage accounting and aggregate arithmetic. It does not repeat the model experiment. Use Python 3.11 or later, install tiktoken , and have the TOMC plugin installed in the Codex profile being tested. Replace the CLI placeholder with your desktop-bundled executable. The runner uses that profile's model, provider and effort; it does not set them. Generating the corpus is offline; the runner makes 36 answering turns plus CPU-only preparation calls. python -m pip install tiktoken python scripts/benchmarks/codex_retention_cases.py --output outputs/codex_cases.json python scripts/benchmarks/codex_retention_run.py --cli "C:/path/to/desktop-bundled/codex.exe" --cases outputs/codex_cases.json --output outputs/codex_retention --concurrency 2 Run the commands from the repository root. Add --resume to the runner to continue completed results in the same output directory. The report helper's export mode ( --results , --cases , --output ) is specific to the recorded October 5 host; its provenance constants need updating for a different setup. The dated recorded data includes corpus and result hashes, per-case scores, budgets, retained-text token counts and provider usage; later reruns can differ.

docs.text: TOMC and other memory tools TOMC changes the representation of selected history before a reader answers. Token compressors choose which text or tokens to retain. Persistent memory systems add storage and retrieval across interactions. These functions can be used at different points in an application. The upstream sources below were reviewed on 2026-09-08. Reviewed revisions and licensing notes are recorded in THIRD_PARTY_LOCK.json . Compilation and compression Method What it retains or constructs Conditioning Reader-facing output Raw Complete input None Original input Truncation A contiguous span Position Kept span Demo BM25 Source lines Query terms Retrieved lines LLMLingua Contexts, sentences and tokens selected by a compressor Prompt components; optional question/instruction Compressed prompt LongLLMLingua Ranked contexts and selected tokens Question Reordered/compressed evidence LLMLingua-2 Tokens selected by a learned model Task-agnostic Selected text TOMC demo State, relation and count records; optional source text Task route Source-linked records and selected text The method distinctions follow the LLMLingua , LongLLMLingua and LLMLingua-2 papers. LLMLingua-2 is task-agnostic by default. TOMC's explicit state replay is limited to its supported operations. The LLMLingua README makes its API easy to try with a short installation and compression example. TOMC likewise provides a small entry point and visible before/after memory. Its ledger adds source references and shows which records fit the budget. The LLMLingua-2 experiment directory separates compression from downstream evaluation; TOMC's benchmark reports are also separate from interactive compilation. Selective Context uses a base model to estimate self-information for lexical units. It provides a Python interface and Streamlit demo. This repository includes neither its implementation nor unrun quality scores. Storage and agents Mem0 provides persistent memory with add/search operations. Letta provides stateful agents and explicit memory management. TOMC's core compiles a supplied history without storing it. The optional MCP integration adds a small local SQLite notebook store. An application could place a compiler between its memory store and reader, but Mem0 and Letta integrations have not been implemented or benchmarked here. What the paper compares The paper evaluates LongLLMLingua, direct and hierarchical LLMLingua-2, BRIEF-Pro, BEAM-RAG and LIGHT with the same three readers. Each row pairs baseline-produced memory with TOMC-produced memory on matched questions. Paper results reports each paired comparison and history length. Overall equal-reader input savings are 34.35% versus hierarchical LLMLingua-2 and 9.32% versus LongLLMLingua. Savings vary by length and baseline. Direct LLMLingua-2 produces 200 empty memories at 1M; its low input therefore does not establish effective compression. The results describe the archived evaluation configurations. The resource table includes a CUDA LLMLingua-2 implementation; it does not establish that LLMLingua-2 requires CUDA. Use the official LLMLingua adapter The optional adapter calls an installed official compressor. It redistributes neither source nor model weights. LLMLingua's MIT license and each selected model's license apply separately. python -m pip install -e '.[llmlingua]' This example initializes a model and may download weights: from llmlingua import PromptCompressor from tomc import compile_memory from tomc.adapters.llmlingua import LLMLinguaAdapter official = PromptCompressor( model_name="microsoft/llmlingua-2-bert-base-multilingual-cased-meetingbank", use_llmlingua2=True, device_map="cpu", ) result = compile_memory( "Your own long context", "Your task", 128, LLMLinguaAdapter(official, variant="llmlingua2"), ) For LLMLingua or LongLLMLingua, supply a compatible official causal compressor and select variant="llmlingua" or "longllmlingua" . The latter forwards the documented question-conditioned ranking and reordering options. If official output exceeds the chosen TOMC counter's budget, the adapter reports additional clipping. The clipped output differs from the untouched official result. Without a configured compressor, it raises AdapterUnavailable instead of substituting another method. See data and licensing for dependency and source records.

LLMLingua's MIT license and each selected model's license apply separately. python -m pip install -e '.[llmlingua]' This example initializes a model and may download weights: from llmlingua import PromptCompressor from tomc import compile_memory from tomc.adapters.llmlingua import LLMLinguaAdapter official = PromptCompressor( model_name="microsoft/llmlingua-2-bert-base-multilingual-cased-meetingbank", use_llmlingua2=True, device_map="cpu", ) result = compile_memory( "Your own long context", "Your task", 128, LLMLinguaAdapter(official, variant="llmlingua2"), ) For LLMLingua or LongLLMLingua, supply a compatible official causal compressor and select variant="llmlingua" or "longllmlingua" . The latter forwards the documented question-conditioned ranking and reordering options. If official output exceeds the chosen TOMC counter's budget, the adapter reports additional clipping. The clipped output differs from the untouched official result. Without a configured compressor, it raises AdapterUnavailable instead of substituting another method. See data and licensing for dependency and source records.
docs.title: Use the official LLMLingua adapter

docs.text: API request optimization and native compaction 中文 · Model limits · API guide Use logical model API requests , not user dialogue turns, as the clock. An agent can make several model requests while handling one user message. AutomaticChatSession provides opt-in preprocessing for a caller-controlled synchronous Chat Completions loop; installing an MCP plugin does not intercept those requests. Simple request policy Cache the documented model profile locally; look it up again only when the request's model ID changes. No repeated provider lookup or extra model judgment is made. Keep provider prompt caches warm. By default ( refresh_policy="stable" ) the compiled old-history memory is frozen: later requests reuse the identical text even when the task changes, and new messages stay raw after it, so consecutive requests share the same prefix. It is rebuilt only when the request would no longer fit, the source history is edited, or the explicit budget changes; set stable_growth_tokens to also rebuild after that much new history. Each rebuild is one full cache miss. refresh_policy="cadence" keeps the earlier behaviour ( refresh_every=2 or 1 ). It rebuilds the memory almost every request in ordinary chats, because the task is the latest user message, and therefore defeats prefix caching: in our measurement it cost several times more than sending the full history with caching. Use it only for providers without prompt caching. Back off once when a context-size hint crosses 50% or 90% of the effective window. For a 1M window these are approximately 500K and 900K. These are TOMC heuristics, not claims about a host's native trigger. Prefer caller-supplied or already available provider usage; the initial string-length fallback is coarse, especially for non-English or multimodal data. When a trusted integration reports native compaction in progress, pass through. After a completed event, skip one or two logical requests (default two), then resume. An ordinary eligible native summary may subsequently be optimized; it has no permanent special exclusion. Model context capacity is not the same as the host's compaction threshold. Account, deployment and configured agent windows can be smaller. Unknown models have no assumed 1M/10M capacity; supply a confirmed deployment_context_limit or keep the request unchanged. Use your existing SDK and model from tomc import AutomaticChatSession session = AutomaticChatSession(native_cooldown_requests=2) # stable, cache-friendly prefix # Reuse one session per conversation; pass the caller's original messages. response = session.create( client, model="deepseek-flash", messages=messages, task="What should the agent do next?", max_tokens=8192, stream=True, ) The same client, credentials, model, tools and request options are forwarded. The raw response or stream is returned unchanged, without extra model calls or consuming the stream. The wrapper changes only messages . Preserve the original history in your application; do not feed an earlier TOMC request view back as the original. Old history gets the existing default memory budget (about 80% of its lexical estimate, at least 1,024), constrained by the model/deployment budget after protected contents and reservations. System/developer instructions, the latest user task, recent messages and pending tool protocol remain unchanged. Complete earlier tool groups are treated together. Unsupported/multimodal/opaque reasoning histories and nonshrinking output pass through. Lexical and string-length estimates are not provider billing counts or a guarantee that every request fits. Specify the desired output limit in the normal SDK request. If it is omitted, output_reserve is a planning hint (8,192 by default), not a change to the provider's actual output limit; provider defaults can be larger, such as Kimi K3's documented 131,072. The wrapper does not silently rewrite output settings. Native events and client scope session.on_native_event("codex", event) recognizes real app-server contextCompaction item start/completion notifications. session.on_native_event("claude", event) recognizes PreCompact / PostCompact hook payloads. A trusted outer integration must route the correct conversation's events. Supported/enabled flags and token-usage updates alone are not compaction events. There is no continuous log polling. This release does not install those listeners, reconfigure Claude Code/Codex/WorkBuddy, or proxy their built-in models. MCP continues to provide explicit external-history preparation and optional notebooks. Its assistant policy leaves the active chat with the host; it is not the request interceptor described above. The initial SDK wrapper supports synchronous, text Chat Completions requests. Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses require their own transport adapters; signed/opaque native compaction items must not be flattened into text. GPT-6.1 Sol tool calling specifically requires Responses according to its model page . CPU scope Decision gating uses counters and cached metadata, with no separate LLM or neural service. The default lexical packing implementation now counts each row once instead of rescanning the growing packed prefix. In one local synthetic state/log fixture, 20K history tokens took 0.026 seconds and 100K took 0.293 seconds for compilation at an 80% memory budget. The earlier implementation took about 1.58 seconds at 20K and 38–47 seconds at 100K. Short randomized counter comparisons and the full 20K fixture preserved text, records and estimates. These are CPU/compiler timings, not real provider latency, billing or answer-quality measurements; they do not establish performance for every history, tokenizer or a 1M input. Claude compact hooks · Codex app-server

docs.text: API 请求优化与原生压缩的配合 English · 模型容量表 · API 指南 统一按 逻辑模型 API 请求次数 计数，不按用户对话轮数。Agent 处理一条用户消息时，可能发出多次模型请求。 AutomaticChatSession 是自己控制请求入口时使用的前置层；安装 MCP 插件不会自动拦截这些请求。 简单规则 模型规格缓存在本地，仅模型 ID 改变时重新对应，不反复查提供商，也不额外调用模型判断。 尽量让提供商的提示词缓存命中。默认（ refresh_policy="stable" ）冻结整理好的旧历史记忆：之后的请求即使任务变了也沿用完全相同的文本，新消息原样接在后面，相邻请求的开头保持一致。只有请求快装不下、原历史被改动或显式预算变化时才重新整理；设置 stable_growth_tokens 后，新增历史超过该值也会重整。每次重整是一次完整的缓存未命中。 refresh_policy="cadence" 保留旧行为（ refresh_every=2 或 1 ）。普通聊天里任务取最新一条用户消息，每轮都不同，所以几乎每次都重新整理，会打断前缀缓存： 实测与模拟 中比“完整历史 + 缓存”贵好几倍。只建议在没有提示词缓存的提供商上使用。 上下文长度提示首次跨过有效窗口的 50% 或 90% 时，各退让一次。1M 模型大约对应 500K、900K。这是 TOMC 的近似避让点，不是宣称宿主的真实触发阈值。优先使用调用方传入或已有 usage；初次字符串长度估算较粗，不能当作精确分词。 收到可信的原生压缩进行中事件时跳过；刚完成后冷却一或两次 API 请求，默认两次，然后恢复。普通、符合处理条件的原生摘要以后可以再次优化，不永久排除。 模型最大容量不等于 Code Agent 的压缩阈值；套餐、部署和客户端设置可能更小。未知模型不会被猜成 1M 或 10M，可用已确认的 deployment_context_limit 指定，否则保持原请求。 接在已有 SDK 前面 from tomc import AutomaticChatSession session = AutomaticChatSession(native_cooldown_requests=2) # 默认稳定前缀，对缓存友好 # 每个会话复用一个 session，传应用保留的原始 messages。 response = session.create( client, model="deepseek-flash", messages=messages, task="下一步 Agent 应该做什么？", max_tokens=8192, stream=True, ) 保留原来的 client、密钥、模型、tools 和请求设置；返回原 response 或 stream，不额外调用模型，也不读取并消耗流。只替换本次请求的 messages 。应用保留完整原始历史，不把上一份 TOMC 发送视图当作原历史继续输入。 旧历史默认沿用约 80% 的词法预算、最低 1,024，并受模型/部署余量限制。系统与开发者指令、当前用户任务、最近消息和未结束的工具协议保留原样；已结束的较旧工具组一起处理。多模态、不支持的消息、不可解释的推理结构、未缩小的输出保持原请求。估计数不是提供商计费数，也不能保证所有请求都不超窗口。 正常在 SDK 请求中指定输出上限。省略时， output_reserve 只是规划余量（默认 8,192），不会改变提供商的实际输出限制；例如 Kimi K3 的公开默认值是 131,072。程序不会悄悄改写输出参数。 与 Code Agent 的接入边界 session.on_native_event("codex", event) 接收真实 app-server contextCompaction 开始/完成事件； session.on_native_event("claude", event) 接收 PreCompact / PostCompact 。外层可信接入负责把正确会话的事件送进来。支持压缩、开启压缩或 usage 更新，不等于压缩事件；不需要持续轮询日志。 本版本没有自动安装这些监听器、修改 Claude Code/Codex/WorkBuddy 设置或代理内置模型。MCP 保留外部历史处理和可选记忆本，其助手规则把当前聊天留给宿主；MCP 本身不是上述请求拦截入口。 首版 SDK 包装器支持同步、文本 Chat Completions；Anthropic Messages 和 OpenAI Responses 需要对应传输适配，不能把签名推理或不透明的原生压缩项直接变成文本。GPT-6.1 Sol 的工具调用要求 Responses，见 官方模型页 。 CPU 开销 判断使用计数器和缓存规格，没有额外 LLM 或神经模型。默认词法打包已改为每行只计数一次，避免反复扫描越来越长的输出。本机同一组合成状态/日志样例中，80% 记忆预算下，20K 历史编译约 0.026 秒、100K 约 0.293 秒；旧实现分别约 1.58 秒、38–47 秒。短随机计数器对照及完整 20K 样例保持文本、记录和估计数一致。这是 CPU/编译计时，不是提供商端到端延迟、计费或回答质量测试，也不代表任意历史、其他分词器或 1M 输入的速度。 Claude 压缩 hooks · Codex app-server

Configure TOMC in Cursor or TRAE 中文 · Assistant setup · Validation record Use TOMC's local stdio MCP server with either client. Earlier checks cover the TOMC backend and Cursor configuration generation; Cursor and TRAE GUI installation and model-selected tool calls remain unverified . This update adds configuration guidance, not a new client test. Use the locked runtime Install UV and make uv available on PATH. Clone the public TOMC repository: git clone https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC.git && printf '
%s
%s
' \ 'If TOMC helps with your work, consider a Star on GitHub (optional):' 'https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC' The Bash / Git Bash command above prints an optional Star invitation after a successful clone. Plain git clone does not show it; cloning alone does not install TOMC. The plugins/claude-code folder contains the shared TOMC source, pyproject.toml , uv.lock and src/server.py . Its runtime can also be registered as a local MCP server in other clients. No Claude Code installation or extra model API key is needed for this route. First startup can download compatible Python and locked dependencies through UV. Before connecting, download the locked dependencies with your actual runtime directory: uv sync --locked --directory "/absolute/path/to/TOMC/plugins/claude-code" Copy the template for Cursor or TRAE . The Cursor template explicitly sets type to stdio , as required by its current configuration reference. Replace both absolute-path placeholders: the runtime directory and its src/server.py file. Use forward slashes in Windows JSON paths, for example C:/Tools/TOMC/plugins/claude-code . Keep the checkout in place; update both paths after moving it. If UV is outside PATH, replace command with its actual executable path. TRAE's documented command restriction excludes spaces in that executable path; directory/script paths belong in separate args strings. Cursor Merge mcpServers.tomc into the project's .cursor/mcp.json or your personal ~/.cursor/mcp.json , preserving existing servers. Restart Cursor and check Customize → MCPs for the tomc server and its five tools. Official MCP configuration . For an existing Python environment installed from current TOMC source with .[mcp] , the alternative python -m tomc setup --client cursor --link prints an Add to Cursor link . It registers that environment; it does not install TOMC or dependencies on another computer. TRAE In the international client, open Settings → MCP , choose the local runtime where a local/cloud choice appears, and add the template through manual JSON configuration. A project configuration uses .trae/mcp.json ; first enable project MCP in Settings → MCP. Preserve other server entries. Official references: international manual/project configuration and Chinese configuration . Menu labels can vary by client edition/version. With .[mcp] installed from current TOMC source, python -m tomc setup --client trae prints an alternative JSON configuration using that environment's absolute Python path. The trae alias is an addition to current source; older ZIP/MCPB previews may not contain it. If this option is unavailable, update the source checkout or use the UV template above. A Python executable path containing spaces conflicts with TRAE's documented command restriction; use the UV template with uv on PATH instead. --link remains Cursor-only. Notebooks and feedback Notebooks default to local plaintext SQLite at ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 . To choose a different file, add env alongside command and args : { "env": {"TOMC_MEMORY_PATH": "/absolute/path/to/tomc-memory.sqlite3"} } Clients sharing that path share explicitly saved notes. TOMC does not collect other chats or provide cloud synchronization. The five tools are prepare_context , remember_memory , recall_memory , list_memories and forget_memory ; storage and deletion require explicit requests. Returned memory enters the host assistant's context and follows its data policy. A tool call does not remove history already held by the host. Please report setup feedback through GitHub issues , including the client/edition, version, OS, configuration route and error message. Omit API keys, private history and notebook contents.

Earlier checks cover the TOMC backend and Cursor configuration generation; Cursor and TRAE GUI installation and model-selected tool calls remain unverified . This update adds configuration guidance, not a new client test.
docs.title: Configure TOMC in Cursor or TRAE

docs.text:
Install UV and make uv available on PATH. Clone the public TOMC repository: git clone https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC.git && printf '
%s
%s
' \ 'If TOMC helps with your work, consider a Star on GitHub (optional):' 'https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC' The Bash / Git Bash command above prints an optional Star invitation after a successful clone. Plain git clone does not show it; cloning alone does not install TOMC. The plugins/claude-code folder contains the shared TOMC source, pyproject.toml , uv.lock and src/server.py . Its runtime can also be registered as a local MCP server in other clients. No Claude Code installation or extra model API key is needed for this route. First startup can download compatible Python and locked dependencies through UV. Before connecting, download the locked dependencies with your actual runtime directory: uv sync --locked --directory "/absolute/path/to/TOMC/plugins/claude-code" Copy the template for Cursor or TRAE . The Cursor template explicitly sets type to stdio , as required by its current configuration reference. Replace both absolute-path placeholders: the runtime directory and its src/server.py file. Use forward slashes in Windows JSON paths, for example C:/Tools/TOMC/plugins/claude-code . Keep the checkout in place; update both paths after moving it. If UV is outside PATH, replace command with its actual executable path. TRAE's documented command restriction excludes spaces in that executable path; directory/script paths belong in separate args strings.
docs.title: Use the locked runtime

docs.text: Merge mcpServers.tomc into the project's .cursor/mcp.json or your personal ~/.cursor/mcp.json , preserving existing servers. Restart Cursor and check Customize → MCPs for the tomc server and its five tools. Official MCP configuration . For an existing Python environment installed from current TOMC source with .[mcp] , the alternative python -m tomc setup --client cursor --link prints an Add to Cursor link . It registers that environment; it does not install TOMC or dependencies on another computer.
docs.title: Cursor

docs.text: In the international client, open Settings → MCP , choose the local runtime where a local/cloud choice appears, and add the template through manual JSON configuration. A project configuration uses .trae/mcp.json ; first enable project MCP in Settings → MCP. Preserve other server entries. Official references: international manual/project configuration and Chinese configuration . Menu labels can vary by client edition/version. With .[mcp] installed from current TOMC source, python -m tomc setup --client trae prints an alternative JSON configuration using that environment's absolute Python path. The trae alias is an addition to current source; older ZIP/MCPB previews may not contain it. If this option is unavailable, update the source checkout or use the UV template above. A Python executable path containing spaces conflicts with TRAE's documented command restriction; use the UV template with uv on PATH instead. --link remains Cursor-only.
docs.title: TRAE

docs.text: Notebooks default to local plaintext SQLite at ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 . To choose a different file, add env alongside command and args : { "env": {"TOMC_MEMORY_PATH": "/absolute/path/to/tomc-memory.sqlite3"} } Clients sharing that path share explicitly saved notes. TOMC does not collect other chats or provide cloud synchronization. The five tools are prepare_context , remember_memory , recall_memory , list_memories and forget_memory ; storage and deletion require explicit requests. Returned memory enters the host assistant's context and follows its data policy. A tool call does not remove history already held by the host. Please report setup feedback through GitHub issues , including the client/edition, version, OS, configuration route and error message. Omit API keys, private history and notebook contents.

docs.text: TOMC Memory for DeepSeek Harness 中文 Unofficial community integration, independently developed and maintained. TOMC connects to DeepSeek Harness (DSH) through the official @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client over local stdio. DSH launches the Python server and exposes its tools as mcp__tomc__<tool> . No fork of DSH is required. Dated validation and test scope . TOMC runs memory preparation on CPU without an additional model service. Your chosen DSH model still performs the assistant's reasoning and answer generation. Use explicitly saved task notes or separately supplied history; the MCP connection does not intercept model requests or replace DSH's active-chat compaction. Install from source Requirements: Git, Python 3.10+ and a Node.js version supported by your DSH release (the validation uses Node.js 24). Configure your model in DSH separately. TOMC itself needs no model API key. Clone the public software repository : git clone https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC.git cd TOMC python -m venv .venv On Windows PowerShell, run: .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e '.[mcp]' .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/setup_deepseek.py --output "$env:USERPROFILE/.tomc/deepseek/tomc.cordis.yml" npx.cmd --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 web --patch "$env:USERPROFILE/.tomc/deepseek/tomc.cordis.yml" On macOS/Linux, the equivalent commands are: .venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[mcp]' .venv/bin/python scripts/setup_deepseek.py --output "$HOME/.tomc/deepseek/tomc.cordis.yml" npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 web --patch "$HOME/.tomc/deepseek/tomc.cordis.yml" The overlay contains absolute paths to your Python and notebook database. Keep the checkout and virtual environment in place. It has no credentials and adds only the TOMC MCP entry. The helper writes UTF-8 and refuses to overwrite an existing file; choose a new output filename if regenerating after a move. Do not distribute your generated configuration as a portable installer. The example pins the DSH version used for validation. DSH is a preview and later versions may change integration APIs. The macOS/Linux commands are provided as equivalents; consult the validation record for actually tested platforms. For an already-installed DSH CLI, replace npx ... web with dsh web . Keep --patch before app-specific flags such as --port . Launch with that overlay each time. For persistent integration, merge its single insert operation into your existing profile's cordis.patch.yml ; never replace an existing patch file that may contain other configuration. Do not register TOMC twice in one profile. For a separate notebook database, add --store /absolute/path/memory.sqlite3 when generating the overlay. To share notes with another assistant, explicitly choose the same database file in both clients. Default storage is ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 , unless TOMC_MEMORY_PATH is configured. Verify in two fresh DSH sessions Open the authenticated local URL printed by DSH and configure a working model. Allow the requested TOMC calls through DSH's normal permission prompts. In session A, send: Use mcp__tomc__remember_memory to save a notebook named dsh-demo: Project Lark uses port 4317. Keep the public API unchanged. Pagination tests are still pending. Show whether the tool succeeded. Create a new session in the same DSH profile, without copying the earlier conversation, and send: Use mcp__tomc__recall_memory on notebook dsh-demo. What port does Project Lark use, what must stay unchanged, and which tests remain? Do not guess. Ask for a next-step checklist based on the recalled constraints. Verify the actual tool result and answer, rather than accepting a claim that it was saved. mcp__tomc__get_status reports runtime settings, while mcp__tomc__list_memories lists available notebook names. To remove the synthetic demo note, explicitly ask to forget only dsh-demo . Data and scope Named notebook writes are explicit. TOMC does not automatically collect the entire DSH chat or inspect your other chats. Successful preparation and recall save prepared context and task text locally by default in TOMC 0.2.1. Context recording can be disabled in TOMC's controls; existing snapshots remain until deleted. Inspect get_status before use. TOMC's processing is local. Tool results selected for the conversation are visible to the DSH model provider, just like other model context. Token estimates refer to prepared memory, not full API billing. Short inputs may remain intact; tool overhead can outweigh savings. This integration does not establish a universal quality, latency, or cost improvement. Removing --patch disconnects this integration on the next launch but does not delete saved notes or context snapshots. Troubleshooting If tools do not appear, inspect DSH startup errors and check that the configured Python still exists and can run -m tomc mcp . Regenerate the overlay if you moved the virtual environment. This is an additive Cordis patch, not an mcpServers JSON file for another client. A DSH page loading while its APIs return HTTP 403 is a browser Host/Origin issue, not evidence that TOMC connected. Keep the printed hostname and port consistent, and inspect browser/proxy rewriting; do not disable DSH's trust checks. The local Windows validation required a loopback port-80 launch because the browser sent an Origin without the non-default port. Use --port 80 only if available and permitted on your system; other machines can use DSH's normal port. Upstream references: MCP client , memory MCP guide , community posting rules .

In session A, send: Use mcp__tomc__remember_memory to save a notebook named dsh-demo: Project Lark uses port 4317. Keep the public API unchanged. Pagination tests are still pending. Show whether the tool succeeded. Create a new session in the same DSH profile, without copying the earlier conversation, and send: Use mcp__tomc__recall_memory on notebook dsh-demo. What port does Project Lark use, what must stay unchanged, and which tests remain? Do not guess. Ask for a next-step checklist based on the recalled constraints. Verify the actual tool result and answer, rather than accepting a claim that it was saved. mcp__tomc__get_status reports runtime settings, while mcp__tomc__list_memories lists available notebook names. To remove the synthetic demo note, explicitly ask to forget only dsh-demo .
docs.title: Verify in two fresh DSH sessions

docs.text: Named notebook writes are explicit. TOMC does not automatically collect the entire DSH chat or inspect your other chats. Successful preparation and recall save prepared context and task text locally by default in TOMC 0.2.1. Context recording can be disabled in TOMC's controls; existing snapshots remain until deleted. Inspect get_status before use. TOMC's processing is local. Tool results selected for the conversation are visible to the DSH model provider, just like other model context. Token estimates refer to prepared memory, not full API billing. Short inputs may remain intact; tool overhead can outweigh savings. This integration does not establish a universal quality, latency, or cost improvement. Removing --patch disconnects this integration on the next launch but does not delete saved notes or context snapshots.

docs.text: If tools do not appear, inspect DSH startup errors and check that the configured Python still exists and can run -m tomc mcp . Regenerate the overlay if you moved the virtual environment. This is an additive Cordis patch, not an mcpServers JSON file for another client. A DSH page loading while its APIs return HTTP 403 is a browser Host/Origin issue, not evidence that TOMC connected. Keep the printed hostname and port consistent, and inspect browser/proxy rewriting; do not disable DSH's trust checks. The local Windows validation required a loopback port-80 launch because the browser sent an Origin without the non-default port. Use --port 80 only if available and permitted on your system; other machines can use DSH's normal port. Upstream references: MCP client , memory MCP guide , community posting rules .

docs.text: DeepSeek Harness integration validation — 2026-10-29 This is a compatibility check of an unofficial community integration, not a benchmark of general answer quality, API cost, or latency. Environment Windows, Node.js 24.15.0, DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 from the official npm package. TOMC 0.2.1 source runtime with MCP 1.30.0 and the additive DSH setup command. Dedicated synthetic notebook databases and DSH home under ignored local output. No manuscript, private conversation, or production notebook was used. Official MCP bridge The reproducible check mounts DSH's real Cordis SystemPrompt , ToolRuntime , and @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client . It starts the TOMC Python stdio server and dispatches through ToolRuntime.execute ; it does not replace the bridge with a mock or a different MCP client. Check Result Discovery All 10 TOMC tools registered under mcp__tomc__ Write Saved the synthetic Project Lark note through DSH Persistence A fresh Cordis context and Python process recalled the note Isolation Unrelated notebook marker absent from recalled memory External history 22,516 estimated input tokens → 495 estimated memory tokens under a 512-token budget; requested port retained Status get_status completed through DSH The deliberately repetitive synthetic history is a transport/budget fixture. Its reduction is not a representative compression rate or measured API saving. This bridge test makes no model inference request . Machine-readable bridge evidence To reproduce, supply the installed DSH package.json , TOMC's Python executable, and a new output directory: node scripts/validate_deepseek_mcp.mjs /absolute/path/to/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/package.json /absolute/path/to/TOMC/.venv/bin/python /absolute/path/to/new-test-output The script creates a synthetic SQLite database; do not point it at existing data. On Windows, use the virtual environment's Scripts/python.exe . Web UI The actual DSH Web profile boots with the generated TOMC overlay. This machine's browser sent an Origin without the non-default port, causing DSH to reject API calls with 403. A loopback port-80 launch restored matching authority and normal UI access. No authentication or trust check was disabled. This local workaround is not a requirement for other installations. Live DeepSeek model test On 2026-10-29, the actual DSH Web UI used the official DeepSeek provider with model route deepseek-flash (UI label: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 1017, reasoning off). This test made real model requests with a working API credential. Session A called mcp__tomc__remember_memory exactly once to save a synthetic Project Cedar notebook. The tool returned saved: true , entries: 1 . A new, separate session B called mcp__tomc__recall_memory exactly once with a 512-token budget. Its prompt supplied only the notebook name and requested fields, not the answers. The model correctly reported all four recorded facts: port 4826, unchanged public API, pending retry tests, and marker cedar-7K29 . A follow-up in session B produced a three-part checklist using the recalled port, API constraint, and pending tests, with no additional tool calls. The marker is synthetic, not a real credential. The official DSH session logs confirm two distinct sessions, the two named TOMC calls, successful tool results, and the model responses. Only these synthetic prompts/results and model routes are included in the sanitized live evidence . System prompts, local paths, credentials, and unrelated runtime metadata are omitted. The short recalled note used the raw path: 41 estimated input tokens → 41 estimated memory tokens, 0% reduction . This verifies cross-session persistence and model use of recalled constraints; it provides no API savings claim and does not test long-history answer quality. DSH's own prompt/tool overhead is separate. Repository checks 50 focused Python tests passed, covering setup generation, MCP calls, delivery limits, and existing integrations. The strict documentation build and generated Claude Code runtime consistency check passed. macOS/Linux DSH operation has not been tested in this run. A separate, newly created Python 3.11 virtual environment also installed .[mcp] from source, generated its own overlay, and passed the same real DSH bridge check. This checks the documented fresh-install path as well as the existing development environment. Installation · 中文安装说明

docs.text: 在 DeepSeek Harness 中使用 TOMC Memory English 非官方社区项目，由社区开发者独立开发和维护。 TOMC 通过 DSH 官方 @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client 的本地 stdio 连接接入，工具名称为 mcp__tomc__<工具名> ，无需修改 DSH 源码。 实测记录与测试范围 。 TOMC 用 CPU 准备任务记忆，不需要额外模型服务。聊天回答仍由你在 DSH 中选择的 模型生成。此接入用于明确保存的笔记和单独提供的外部历史，不接管 DSH 的原生聊天压缩， 也不自动拦截 API 请求。 Windows 安装 准备 Git、Python 3.10+ 和 DSH 支持的 Node.js；本次验证使用 Node.js 24。 在 PowerShell 中执行： git clone https://github.com/ZipengWu365/TOMC.git cd TOMC python -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e '.[mcp]' .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/setup_deepseek.py --output "$env:USERPROFILE/.tomc/deepseek/tomc.cordis.yml" npx.cmd --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5 web --patch "$env:USERPROFILE/.tomc/deepseek/tomc.cordis.yml" 打开 DSH 输出的本地地址，在 DSH 内单独配置模型。TOMC 本身无需 API Key。 macOS/Linux 命令见英文说明；平台测试范围以验证记录为准。 生成文件仅追加 TOMC MCP 配置，包含本机 Python 和数据库的绝对路径，不含密钥。 保留仓库和虚拟环境的目录位置；移动后使用新文件名重新生成。生成器拒绝覆盖已有文件。 每次启动保留 --patch ，也可将其中单个 insert 操作合并进已有 DSH profile 的 cordis.patch.yml ，不要覆盖原有配置，也不要重复注册同一服务。 可通过生成器的 --store 指定独立数据库。默认是 ~/.tomc/memory.sqlite3 （ TOMC_MEMORY_PATH 可覆盖）；要和其他助手共享笔记，需要明确配置同一个数据库文件。 实际验证 在会话 A 中输入： 调用 mcp__tomc__remember_memory，保存笔记 dsh-demo：Project Lark 使用端口 4317，公共 API 必须保持不变，分页测试尚未完成。请展示工具是否保存成功。 新建会话 B，不复制会话 A 的内容，然后输入： 调用 mcp__tomc__recall_memory 读取 dsh-demo。这个项目使用哪个端口、什么不能改、 还缺哪些测试？请根据工具返回回答，不要猜测。 最后让模型根据召回内容列出下一步清单。检查实际工具调用和结果，而不只是模型口头声称成功。 按 DSH 的正常权限提示允许相关操作。 mcp__tomc__get_status 可检查运行设置； mcp__tomc__list_memories 可查看笔记名。删除演示笔记时，明确指定只忘记 dsh-demo 。 存储与限制 保存笔记需要明确调用，TOMC 不自动收集整段 DSH 聊天，也不能查看其他会话。 0.2.1 默认将成功准备／召回后的上下文和任务存入本地上下文库；可在 TOMC 控制中 关闭记录，既有快照不会自动删除。先用 get_status 检查设置。 TOMC 在本机处理数据；返回给聊天的工具内容会进入你选择的模型服务商的上下文。 词元数是记忆文本估算，不是完整 API 账单。短输入可能原样保留，工具调用也有开销。 本次接入不证明所有任务都省钱、提速或提高回答质量。 下次启动去掉 --patch 即不再加载此接入；已保存的笔记和快照会保留。 若工具没有出现，检查启动日志和配置里的 Python 路径。本文件是 Cordis 追加配置， 不是其他客户端的 mcpServers JSON。 若网页能打开但接口报 403，检查浏览器是否改变了 Origin 的主机或端口，不要关闭 DSH 的安全检查。本机 Windows 验证遇到浏览器省略 Origin 端口，改为本地 --port 80 后恢复；仅在该端口空闲且系统允许时使用。正常环境可使用 DSH 默认端口。 DSH 官方 MCP 文档 · 官方社区分享规则
